options.text: Async, because the call mostly waits.
options.why: Right. Concurrency is about waiting, so a call that waits fits async.

options.text: Processes, because they are always faster.
options.why: No. This course does not claim speed for any tool here.

options.text: No tool, because a call that waits needs none.
options.why: No. The call still needs a way to wait beside other calls.

question: A tool call sends a web request and waits for the reply. In this course's model, which tool fits?

options.text: The two that only read; the writer runs alone.
options.why: Right. Safe calls may overlap, and the writer changes shared state, so it runs one at a time.

options.text: All three, because they are all calls.
options.why: No. The writer changes shared state, so it may not overlap.

options.text: None, because a read is unsafe.
options.why: No. A read that changes nothing is safe to overlap.

question: Two calls only read data, and a third writes a shared file. Which calls may overlap?

options.text: A bug where the result depends on which of two steps runs first.
options.why: Right. The snippet's final value depends on the order of the steps.

options.text: A program that crashes at random.
options.why: No. A race is about order, not crashing.

options.text: Two files with the same name.
options.why: No. A race concerns the order of steps on shared data.
